title: Green wins Nürburgring Race 2 as Rast’s third place clinches the DTM title
dek: Jamie Green won from pole by 0.442 seconds for Audi Sport Team Rosberg, and René Rast’s third place made him champion with one round to spare.

chapters.title: Saturday leaves Rast needing nine points more than Müller
text: Saturday had gone René Rast’s way. He took pole and his sixth win of the season, while Nico Müller jumped the start, served a drive-through and finished last of the classified runners without a point, leaving Rast 47 points clear on 262 to 215. Bruno Spengler and Marco Wittmann gave BMW a double podium after Mike Rockenfeller’s Audi retired with an oil leak while running second. The sums for Sunday were simple: Rast had to take nine points more than Müller across qualifying and the race to be champion with the Hockenheim finale still to come.

chapters.title: Green takes pole by a thousandth of a second
text: Jamie Green took his second pole position of the year, 1m20.032s, a mere 0.001s faster than Rast’s 1m20.033s. Rast had led after the first runs and improved in the final minute, but Green, only fourth in the first half of the session, deposed him at the last moment and prevented him from collecting the full three points for pole. Rast scored two, stretching his championship lead to 49 points, and said his lap had not been completely clean.

Müller needed a strong grid slot and did not get it. He was 14th, 0.463s off pole, and explained that a sensor problem in his first run and a small mistake at the chicane had spoiled his chances. The sums were now clear: if Rast outscored Müller by seven more points in the race, the title was his a round early, since only 56 points were available at Hockenheim. Rockenfeller was third on 1m20.107s, ahead of Frijns and Aberdein, who was fifth at the end of his strongest DTM weekend, and Duval sixth. Timo Glock was seventh in the best BMW, with Wittmann, Spengler and Sheldon van der Linde eighth to tenth.

Ferdinand Habsburg was the quickest Aston Martin in 15th, 0.601s off pole. Paul di Resta set no time because his crew spent the session working on a technical problem with the car, and he did not take the start.

chapters.title: Rast leads, van der Linde punts Glock
text: Rast made a perfect getaway from second and passed Green on the run to Turn 1, which made the title look nearly won. Green, however, never fell more than a second behind him over the opening phase. Behind them Rockenfeller and Duval ran third and fourth, with Frijns and Aberdein next.

On the second lap van der Linde ran into the back of his BMW team-mate Glock on the way to the first corner and spun him. Glock dropped from eighth to the back of the field, and van der Linde was given a drive-through penalty. Müller, who had lost a place to Habsburg at the start and won it back, gained two places from the BMW tangle and had reached the top ten by lap nine.

chapters.title: Green undercuts Rast, Müller gambles on an early stop
text: Müller was one of the first to make his mandatory stop, around lap ten, hoping for a safety car after a similar gamble had failed on Saturday. Glock and Pietro Fittipaldi followed on lap 11. Rast stopped on lap 12 and Green a lap later, and the Rosberg garage decided the lead: Green’s stop took 7.4s, about 1.5s quicker than Rast’s, and he rejoined ahead.

Rast tried for several laps to pass Green while the Briton was warming his tyres, but could not make a move stick. Müller meanwhile ran fourth on his old tyres, close enough to keep the championship alive by a single point on the road. By lap 21 all of the Audi drivers had changed tyres. Frijns, who stopped on lap 17, would have the freshest tyres for the final laps.

chapters.title: Green holds off Frijns while Rast hangs on to the title
text: Frijns passed Müller at Turn 1 on lap 24, took Duval a lap later and, lapping about half a second faster than Rast, closed up to the Rosberg car and passed him at the chicane on lap 34. Wittmann, the only retirement, came into the pits after 29 laps with a technical problem that had first slowed him at the Mercedes Arena bend. Two laps from the end Aberdein passed Müller on the run to the Coca-Cola Kurve, dropping him to sixth and ensuring that Rast’s third place was enough.

Frijns then attacked Green for the lead at the chicane on the penultimate lap but ran wide across the grass and had to give the place back. Green won by 0.442s, with Rast 5.827s behind in third. Duval, Aberdein, Müller and Rockenfeller made it an all-Audi top seven, Philipp Eng was the best BMW in eighth, ahead of Glock, who recovered from the spin, and Spengler. Daniel Juncadella was the best Aston Martin in 12th and van der Linde finished 16th after his penalty. Rast set the fastest lap, a 1m22.253s on lap four.

chapters.title: A second title for Rast and a first win in two years for Green
text: Rast was champion with 279 points, 56 clear of Müller, with a round still to run. On the slowing-down lap he asked, disbelieving, whether he was now champion; he had not known that Müller finished only sixth. He said afterwards that he was not satisfied with the race itself, but that the title had been the target, and thanked Audi Sport and his team. Audi’s motorsport chief, Dieter Gass, said he had not expected the championship to come so early and wondered where the BMWs had gone.

Green ended a wait of almost two years for a DTM victory. He said it was a hard race, in which Frijns’s late attack on better tyres had been difficult to resist, and that, although Audi’s drivers worked together, on Sunday they had been allowed to fight and he was the winner. Müller conceded the title fight gracefully, saying the team had known it would be hard to beat Rast and had needed help, and that the early stop had been his only chance to move forward.

For BMW the day was unsatisfactory after Saturday’s double podium. Motorsport director Jens Marquardt congratulated Rast and Audi on a deserved title, then pointed to the unnecessary collision between van der Linde and Glock and to Wittmann’s retirement, and said eighth, ninth and tenth were not enough. Wittmann, who had arrived with a mathematical chance of the title, was now out of the picture.

The season finale follows at the Hockenheimring on 4–6 October. Three Super GT wildcards will run there on the same Hankook tyres as the DTM field: Jenson Button in a Honda for both races, and Lexus and Nissan crews sharing the drives, one driver per race. The Super GT cars cannot use the drag reduction system and cannot score points.

facts.t: Title with a round to spare
facts.v: René Rast’s third place gave him his second DTM title with 279 points, 56 clear of Nico Müller, with one round still to run.
